You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:

paragraphs.text: 13. ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE

13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.

13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.

13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.

13.4 Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.

Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].

- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 gives Customer an unconditional right to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form without cause, and Section 29.4 fixes that notice at thirty days before the effective termination date, meeting the preferred 30-day standard. Customer owes only accrued Fees (no early-termination fee or penalty anywhere in Sections 7, 9, 10 or 11), and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, which is a pro-rata refund (reinforced by Section 10.2). No provision anywhere grants Vendor any termination-for-convenience or without-cause right during the three-year term (Section 8.1); Vendor's termination rights are limited to material breach (9.1) and insolvency (9.2), and even the non-renewal mechanic in Section 8.2 is Customer-only. The clause therefore meets the preferred position in full.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.",
  "Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.",
  "Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.",
  "Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.",
  "Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.",
  "Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.",
  "Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.",
  "Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.",
  "The parties do not jointly own intellectual property."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.",
  "Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.",
  "Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.",
  "Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.",
  "Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.",
  "Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.",
  "Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.",
  "Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services."
]

Every preferred element is met in operative language: the cap is expressly mutual, the basis is now the greater of fees paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, the indirect/consequential exclusion is bilateral, and the Excluded Claims list already carries all seven required uncapped categories.

The payment carve-out is repaired at the right level of generality: it now reaches "Customer's payment obligations" as a whole rather than the narrowly defined subset of Fees, satisfying the definition-resolution requirement for Customer-payment carve-outs.

Minimality holds. Only the two defective phrases were touched (cap basis in 21.1 and the Fees-limited payment sentence in 21.3). The drafter avoided the cleaner-looking but broader route of rewriting §1.5/§1.6 by using lower-case "fees" scoped to the Agreement and all Order Forms; "and all Order Forms" is necessary rather than surplus because the original expressly confined the cap to the first Order Form. No survival tails, procedures, expense language or extra damages categories were added, and no explanatory examples were bolted onto the formula.

Intent is preserved: the mutual "regardless of the form of action or number of claims" sentence, the Customer-favourable direct-damages sentence in 21.2 (data restoration, replacement services, notices, incident response), and the "undisputed"/"conforming Services" qualifier all survive without contradiction; the retained §1.5/§1.6 definitions still function elsewhere and leave no dangling cross-reference or undefined term.

Optional polish only, not a defect: the coexistence of defined "Fees" (Implementation Fee only) and lower-case "fees" in 21.1 could be made airtight with a short parenthetical such as "(regardless of the definition of 'Fees' in Section 1.5)", but the current self-describing formulation is unambiguous and adding it would risk non-minimality.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:

**Finding: COMPLIANT (preferred)** — no redline proposed.

§ 8.2 and § 8.3 together meet every preferred element:
- **12-month renewal terms** — "renews for successive twelve-month periods" (no multi-year auto-renewal).
- **30-day opt-out** — "at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal," and Customer's deadline is extended if Vendor misses its reminder.
- **60-day Vendor reminder** — "Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand."
- **Uplift cap** — "only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index ... and three percent," plus 90 days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods.

§ 7 (Fees) and § 9 (Termination) carry no competing renewal or uplift mechanic, so the rule is fully satisfied without amendment.

Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.
input.rationale: Section 28 sits at our preferred position: New York law governs the Agreement and every dispute arising from it (28.1), and the state and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction with irrevocable submission and a venue/forum-non-conveniens waiver (28.2). The only other-court carve-out is the customary one for temporary injunctive relief to protect confidential information or IP, which does not defeat the exclusive merits forum. There is no arbitration clause anywhere in the document (Sections 29 and 30 and the remaining sections contain no dispute forum terms); 28.3's pre-filing executive escalation is a short good-faith step that expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings, so it does not displace the court forum. No redline needed.

paragraphs.text: 24. ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL

24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.

24.2 Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.

24.3 For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.

24.4 Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.

payload.text: 1.1 “Affiliate” means, with respect to a Party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Party. “Control” means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of an entity or the power to direct its management. An entity is an Affiliate only while that relationship continues.

Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.

content.text:
**Finding: T4C — compliant (preferred level).**

- **Customer convenience right:** § 9.4 lets Customer terminate the Agreement *or any Order Form* without cause; § 29.4 sets that notice at **thirty days**, matching the preferred 30-day standard.
- **No penalty:** Customer "owes only accrued Fees." No early-termination fee, wind-down charge, or penalty appears in § 7 (Fees), § 10 (Effect of Termination), or § 11 (Transition).
- **Pro-rata refund:** § 9.4 requires refund of prepaid Fees for the period after termination, reinforced by § 10.2 (prepaid recurring Fees covering the post-termination period).
- **No Vendor convenience right:** Across the document Vendor may terminate only for material breach (§ 9.1) and insolvency (§ 9.2). The § 8.2 renewal opt-out is Customer-only, and § 24.4 bars termination on Customer change of control — so nothing gives Vendor a mid-term walk-away during the three-year term (§ 8.1).

No redline proposed; the clause sits at our preferred position.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

paragraphs.text: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

**Finding: compliant (GOVLAW) — no redline.**

Section 28 meets the preferred position in full:
- **§28.1** — New York law governs the Agreement and each dispute arising from it (with CISG excluded).
- **§28.2** — Exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, plus irrevocable submission to personal jurisdiction and waiver of venue/inconvenient-forum objections. The carve-out permitting temporary injunctive relief in another court is the customary one and does not undercut the exclusive merits forum.

No arbitration provision exists anywhere in the document, and §28.3's pre-filing executive escalation expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings, so it does not displace the court forum.

Kind: missing

paragraphs.text: 14. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES

14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.

14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.

14.3 Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.

14.4 No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.

ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.

Category: audit

No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

  "The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.",
  "Audits are conducted off-site where possible.",
  "Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.",

paragraphs.text: 21. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.

21.2 Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.

21.3 “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

21.4 The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

paragraphs.text: 7. FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES

7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.

7.2 Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.

7.3 Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.

7.4 Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.

7.5 Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.
7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.

7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
4. ORDER FORMS AND AFFILIATE ORDERS

4.1 An Order Form becomes binding when signed by both Parties. Changes in scope, assumptions, quantities, Fees, dependencies, or dates require a written change order signed by authorized representatives. Vendor shall not charge for work outside scope that Customer did not approve in a signed change order.

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:

Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

[

  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",

  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",

Parties: we represent Northwind Analytics, Inc.; counterparty is Brightline Cloud Services Ltd..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.",
  "Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.",
  "Audits occur during business hours.",
  "Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.",
  "The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.",
  "Audits are conducted off-site where possible.",
  "Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.",
  "Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor may audit no more than once per year.",
  "Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.",
  "Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent."
]
